purpose: Turn competence and risk signals into assignment decisions with capability matching, exploration floors, confidence-aware choices, human escalation thresholds, and auditable traces.
assumptions: Competence vectors and breaker states are available
Tasks carry type SIZE RISK pattern fields
exclusions: Kubernetes pod scheduling as primary scope

competency_questions.question: What is the routing objective and how is the eligibility set built?
How does the exploration floor work numerically?
How are capability match and xverify split enforced?
How do canaries and starvation controls protect recovery?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: half-open only S canaries; 14d starvation boost

competency_questions.question: How do confidence/CI width and decision traces affect routing?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ECE and ci_width rules; trace schema; optional shadow

competency_questions.question: What human escalation thresholds and risk floors apply?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: numeric escalation triggers and HIGH trust floor example

competency_questions.question: How do load caps, SLA priority, and backpressure interact?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: concurrency caps; priority order; queue threshold action

competency_questions.question: What may half-open agents receive and how is risk gated?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: S canaries only; HIGH floors; split roles

competency_questions.question: How are pool awards audited against starvation?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: award rules deny invalid claims; traces and share metrics

competency_questions.question: How are reassigns and policy changes governed?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: revise reassign rules; sim gate on policy change; filter order

glossary.definition: Agents passing breaker risk load and lane predicates
Minimum fraction of assigns to non-leader eligible agents (>=1/5)
Breaker state allowing only canary S tasks
Selecting by task_type lane trust among eligible
Logged candidates filters trusts and chosen rule path
Minimum trust and n required for a RISK class
Eligible agent receiving far below floor share
Counterfactual assignee without exploration for offline eval
Fixed sequence of routing filters for determinism

source_registry.description: heuristic priors for multi-agent routing decisions aligned with EXCHANGE scoring scaffold
source_registry.citation_or_locator: heuristic prior; operational scoring practice; no external dataset supplied

nodes.definition: Route each task to maximize expected successful accept under constraints: lane competence match, exploration floor, breaker state, load, and human-escalation risk. Objective is not lowest latency alone and not pure favoritism to current leader.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: router always picks the globally highest trust ignoring lane and breakers

pros.example: utility uses lane trust and constraints

cons.claim: Misspecified utility can still starve recovery

nodes.definition: Match task_type to agent competence_vector lane trust. Require candidate breaker_state=closed (or half-open canary). Prefer argmax trust among eligible, subject to exploration floor.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: content task assigned to agent with only verify-lane evidence

cons.claim: Cold start agents never eligible without prior blend

acceptance_tests: eligibility: lane key + breaker closed/half-open rules

nodes.definition: Never give 100 percent of a lane to the current leader. Reserve exploration floor >=1 in 5 assignments (20 percent) for a lower-scored ACTIVE eligible agent or recovering half-open canary, so bad streaks can be broken and metrics stay identifiable.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: leader takes every content task for a month; others starve

pros.claim: Floor prevents monopoly and enables recovery data

cons.claim: Floor can reduce short-term accept rate

acceptance_tests: floor fraction documented and enforced in router

nodes.definition: When combining multi-judge axis scores, weight by calibrated confidence only if ECE<=0.15; else equal weight. For routing, treat ci_width on trust as uncertainty: if width>0.25, reduce exploitation preference and increase exploration probability for that agent.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: router treats uncalibrated 0.99 confidence as certainty

acceptance_tests: ECE and ci_width policies in router

nodes.definition: Escalate to human when: safety/scope conflict unresolved; two agents disagree on high-stakes ACCEPT with |Q diff|>=2.0; trust of only eligible agent <0.40 with n>=5; or breaker would leave lane with zero eligible agents. Default response SLA target 24h for MED tasks.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: pipeline silently assigns despite zero eligible agents

nodes.definition: Cap concurrent in_progress tasks per agent (default 1 build + 1 verify, or 2 total). Prefer eligible idle agents among top trust tier. Prevents queue pileup and context thrash.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: same agent given five concurrent builds

cons.claim: Caps can idle capacity if set too low

nodes.definition: Half-open agents only receive canary-tagged tasks (size S, clear gates). Success closes breaker; failure re-opens. Canaries count toward exploration floor. Never send SIZE L to half-open.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: half-open agent receives full MED content rewrite

acceptance_tests: half-open may only take canary S tasks

nodes.definition: When trusts within 0.03, break ties by: lower current load, then longer time since last assign (fairness), then higher ci_width exploration need, then stable hash of task_id. Prevents silent leader lock-in on near-ties.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: 0.01 trust edge always wins forever

nodes.definition: Log each assignment: task_id, candidates, eligibility filters, trusts, exploration flag, chosen agent, rule path. Traces enable audit and debugging of starvation or bias.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: cannot explain why agent B never receives tasks

nodes.definition: Map SIZE/RISK to priority: safety and protocol tasks first; then HIGH risk; MED default; S canaries fill exploration. SLA targets example: HIGH 12h, MED 24h, S 48h for first response assignment.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: canary S jumps ahead of safety-critical protocol task

nodes.definition: For single+xverify patterns, route builder by content/code lane trust and xverify by verify-lane trust with different agent than builder. Never assign same agent both roles on same task.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: builder also assigned as xverify on own delivery

pros.claim: Split roles enforce no self-grade structurally

cons.claim: With only two agents limited pairs

acceptance_tests: pattern rules forbid builder equals xverify

nodes.definition: When tasks are POOL, agents may claim; integrator awards by eligibility, trust, load, and exploration needs. Claims are data not self-assignment of authority. Deny claims that violate breaker or lane mismatch.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: first claim auto-wins regardless of breaker

acceptance_tests: award algorithm uses eligibility trust load exploration

nodes.definition: Monitor tasks_assigned per agent per lane over 14d; flag starvation if eligible agent receives < floor share minus epsilon. Auto-boost exploration probability next window.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: eligible agent gets zero tasks for 14 days

pros.claim: Starvation metrics close the loop on floor policy

nodes.definition: HIGH risk tasks require higher trust floor (example trust>=0.60 and n>=5) or human co-sign. MED default trust>=0.45 or prior blend. S canaries allow half-open. Risk gating prevents novices on dangerous mutations.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: n=1 agent assigned HIGH risk protocol change

nodes.definition: On REVISE, default same agent if revise_count<2 and breaker closed; else consider reassign to higher-trust eligible peer. On repeated FAIL, reassign or escalate. Lane correction reassigns when evidence shows wrong lane (content authoring misroutes).

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: third identical revise stays with same failing approach forever

cons.example: prefer same agent for first revise

nodes.definition: Optionally compute counterfactual assignee (who would have been chosen without exploration) and log for offline evaluation of floor tax. Shadow mode does not change live assignment.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: cannot measure cost of exploration floor

nodes.definition: Apply filters in order: (1) hard denials/pattern constraints (2) breaker eligibility (3) risk floors (4) concurrency caps (5) lane match (6) exploration floor lottery (7) tie-break. Ordering makes behavior predictable and testable.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: filters applied in random order yielding unstable assigns

cons.claim: Rigid order may need rare overrides

nodes.definition: If unassigned queue exceeds threshold (example 10 MED), raise exploration temporarily to idle eligible agents, or escalate for more capacity. Backpressure prevents silent queue growth.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: queue of 25 tasks with no alert

nodes.definition: Before changing floor fractions or trust floors, simulate on historical decision traces. Reject policy changes that increase predicted FAIL rate >5 percent absolute without human approval.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: floor changed live to 50 percent without simulation

cons.claim: Historical traces miss new task types

acceptance_tests: policy change requires sim or explicit waiver

nodes.definition: Build candidate set as agents where: active status, breaker allows, risk floor met, concurrency available, lane defined. Empty set => human escalation, never force ineligible assign.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: router assigns DEGRADED agent because set building skipped

pros.claim: Eligibility set is hard safety boundary

edges.why_related: always pick best vs force exploration
edges.resolution_rule: argmax among eligible except floor slots for challenger/canary

edges.why_related: HIGH risk floors vs need to explore novices
edges.resolution_rule: explore on MED/S; HIGH requires trust floors or human

edges.why_related: spread load vs meet priority SLA

conflict_axes.name: exploit_vs_explore
conflict_axes.description: Best agent vs floor for others

conflict_axes.name: load_vs_sla
conflict_axes.description: Spread work vs hit priority SLA

conflict_axes.name: same_agent_revise_vs_reassign
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: same for first revise; then consider reassign

conflict_axes.name: sim_gate_vs_agility
conflict_axes.description: Require sim vs flip policy fast
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: sim or waiver on policy change

edge_cases.description: Policy floor flipped live without sim

workflow.description: Argmax or challenger via ordered filters
Pick distinct verifier if pattern needs

priority_rationale: Eligibility and role-split dominate convenience; exploration floors dominate pure exploitation; escalation dominates forced ineligible assigns.

required_checks: all edge ids unique EDGE_XXX format
all from/to in edges reference valid node ids
all competency_question_refs resolve to valid CQ ids
all evidence_refs resolve to valid source_registry ids
all priority_order entries are valid node ids with no duplicates
high_risk_nodes (risk_if_wrong>=0.80) have non-empty acceptance_tests and human_review_required=true
conflict edges have signed_tension<0 and resolution_rule present
observed_impact=0.0 for all nodes (no observed data)
19-24 nodes, 32-40 edges, 8-10 conflict_axes, 10-12 edge_cases, 9-12 workflow steps
post_formula_checks: all derived fields non-zero after compute run
